extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Rules for claiming benefit of prior-filed applications under 35 U.S.C. 120/121/365(c)/386(c) (including timing, required identification, petitions for delayed claims, and related ownership issues) and detailed formal standards for drawings submitted in U.S. patent applications (content, format, paper, views, numbering, shading, symbols, photographs, color, corrections, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific reference required by 35 U.S.C. 120
rubrics_metrics.description: The later-filed application must include a reference identifying the prior application by application number (series code and serial number), international application number and international filing date, or international registration number and filing date under § 1.1023.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the later-filed application is a nonprovisional application, the reference must be included in an application data sheet (§ 1.76(b)(5)). The reference must identify the relationship of the applications (continuation, divisional, or continuation-in-part).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for submitting 35 U.S.C. 120 references
rubrics_metrics.description: The reference required by 35 U.S.C. 120 and paragraph (d)(2) must be submitted during the pendency of the later-filed application and meet specific additional time limits depending on filing route.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a), submit within the later of four months from actual filing date or sixteen months from filing date of prior-filed application. For a nonprovisional entering national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371, submit within the later of four months from national stage commencement date or sixteen months from prior-filed filing date (with other specified four-month alternatives). Time periods do not apply to design applications, applications filed under 111(a) before Nov 29, 2000, or international applications filed under 363 before Nov 29, 2000.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to timely submit reference = waiver
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in paragraph (e), failure to timely submit the reference required by 35 U.S.C. 120 and paragraph (d)(2) is considered a waiver of any benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c) to the prior-filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If untimely, applicant may seek relief only under paragraph (e) (petition to accept unintentionally delayed claim) with required documentation and fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for continued prosecution counts as specific reference
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for a continued prosecution application under § 1.53(d) is the specific reference required by 35 U.S.C. 120 to the prior-filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification by application number under this section identifies every application assigned that application number for the specific reference required by 35 U.S.C. 120.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-references in application data sheet (ADS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-references to other related applications may be made when appropriate, but cross-references to applications for which no benefit is claimed under title 35 must not be included in an application data sheet (§ 1.76(b)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.14 for making cross-references where appropriate; avoid listing unrelated applications in the ADS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement for applications with mixed pre- and post-Mar 16, 2013 effective filing dates
rubrics_metrics.description: If a nonprovisional filed on/after Mar 16, 2013 claims benefit of an earlier nonprovisional or international app filed prior to Mar 16, 2013, and also contains (or contained) a claim with an effective filing date on/after Mar 16, 2013, the applicant must provide a statement to that effect within specified time periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement due within the later of four months from actual filing date of later-filed app, four months from entry into national stage (§1.491), sixteen months from filing date of prior-filed app, or the date a first claim with effective filing date on/after Mar 16, 2013 is presented. Exceptions: not required if an earlier-filed app already contains the statement, or if designated individuals reasonably believe no such claim exists or existed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified copy and translation for foreign-language international applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Where benefit is claimed under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c) to an international application or international design application that designates but did not originate in the U.S., the Office may require a certified copy and an English translation if filed in another language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office discretion to request certified copy and translation when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to accept unintentionally delayed benefit claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reference required by 35 U.S.C. 120 is presented after the time period, a claim for benefit may be accepted if the reference was unintentionally delayed and a petition is filed under paragraph (e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition must be accompanied by: (1) the required reference unless previously submitted; (2) the petition fee (§ 1.17(m)) and the applicable fee (§ 1.17(w)); and (3) a statement that the entire delay between due date and filing date was unintentional. Director may require additional information where delay intent is in question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elimination of patentably indistinct claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Where two or more applications filed by the same applicant or assignee contain patentably indistinct claims, elimination of such claims from all but one application may be required absent good and sufficient reason for retention in more than one application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is applied during pendency to prevent duplicate claims across multiple applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements when patents/applications under reexamination name different inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application or a patent under reexamination and at least one other application naming different inventors are owned by the same person and contain patentably indistinct claims, and there is no record indicating common ownership on the effective filing date (or date of invention), the Office may require a statement about common ownership or assignment and, if not commonly owned, identification of the prior inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when commonly owned or assigned, patentably indistinct claims may be rejected under the doctrine of double patenting in view of such commonly owned or assigned applications or patents under reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Older-applications exception for presenting specific reference
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed before Sept 16, 2012, the requirement that any specific reference to a prior-filed application be presented in an ADS will be satisfied by presentation of such specific reference in the first sentence(s) of the specification following the title in the nonprovisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This exception does not apply to specific references submitted for petitions to restore the benefit of a provisional application under paragraph (b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions in international applications may be filed later
rubrics_metrics.description: If a petition under paragraph (b), (c), or (e) is required in an international application not filed with the U.S. Receiving Office and not a nonprovisional, the petition may be filed in the earliest nonprovisional application that claims benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120/121/365(c)/386(c) to the international application and will be treated as filed in the international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows filing of required petitions in later national-stage or subsequent nonprovisional that claims benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefit under 35 U.S.C. 386(c) effective date limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Benefit under 35 U.S.C. 386(c) with respect to an international design application is applicable only to nonprovisional applications, international applications, and international design applications filed on or after May 13, 2015, and patents issuing thereon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not claim 386(c) benefit for earlier filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings required where necessary for understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant is required to furnish a drawing of the invention where necessary for understanding of the subject matter sought to be patented; original drawings should be retained by applicant for future correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111 on or after Dec 18, 2013 for the current rule; see pre-AIA and transitional paragraphs for other filing-date ranges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted drawing content (flow sheets, diagrams)
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings may include illustrations which facilitate an understanding of the invention (for example, flow sheets in cases of processes, and diagrammatic views).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use such illustrations when they aid comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner can require drawings when optional
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever the nature of the subject matter admits of illustration by a drawing without its being necessary for understanding, and applicant has not furnished such a drawing, the examiner will require its submission within not less than two months from the date of notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such compliance is subject to § 1.81(d) regarding corrections and use of drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings cannot cure insufficiency of specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings submitted after the filing date may not be used to overcome any insufficiency of the specification due to lack of an enabling disclosure or otherwise inadequate disclosure, or to supplement the original disclosure for interpretation of the scope of any claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on post-filing drawings to add new disclosure or amend the original enabling description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings must show every claimed feature
rubrics_metrics.description: The drawing in a nonprovisional application must show every feature of the invention specified in the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conventional features whose detailed illustration is not essential may be illustrated by graphical symbols or labeled representations (e.g., labeled rectangular box). Tables and sequences included in the specification should not be duplicated in the drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings for improvements on old machines
rubrics_metrics.description: When the invention is an improvement on an old machine, the drawing must, when possible, exhibit the improved portion disconnected from the old structure, and also show enough of the old structure to show the connection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide views that clarify the improved part both alone and in situ relative to the old structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner may require additional illustration for noncompliant drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Where drawings in a nonprovisional application do not comply with requirements to show claimed features or adequately illustrate improvements, the examiner shall require additional illustration within not less than two months from the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections to such drawings are subject to § 1.81(d) (drawings submitted after filing cannot cure certain deficiencies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable categories for drawings (black ink and color)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two acceptable categories for presenting drawings in utility and design patent applications: (1) Black ink (India ink or equivalent solid black lines) normally required; (2) Color drawings permitted in design applications and rarely in utility applications with petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Color drawings in utility apps only accepted after petition explaining necessity; color drawings not permitted in international applications (PCT Rule 11.13).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for petitions to accept color drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Petition to accept color drawings must include the fee (§ 1.17(h)), one set of color drawings if submitted via USPTO electronic filing system (or three sets if not), and an amendment inserting specified language as the first paragraph of the brief description of the drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The required inserted language notifies that the file contains at least one drawing executed in color and that copies with color drawings will be provided upon request and payment of fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographs permitted only when practicable medium
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs (including photocopies) are not ordinarily permitted in utility and design applications but will be accepted if photographs are the only practicable medium for illustrating the claimed invention (e.g., gels, blots, micrographs, animals, plants, in vivo imaging, crystalline structures, or ornamental effects in design patents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the subject admits of illustration by a drawing, the examiner may require a drawing instead. Photographs must be of sufficient quality that all details are reproducible in the printed patent. Color photographs allowed only if color drawing/photo conditions are satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of drawings on each sheet
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifying indicia should be provided and should include title of the invention, inventor’s name, and application number or docket number (if any) if an application number has not been assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If provided, this information must be placed on the front of each sheet within the top margin. Each drawing sheet submitted after filing must be identified as 'Replacement Sheet' or 'New Sheet' pursuant to § 1.121(d). Marked-up copies with annotations must be clearly labeled 'Annotated Sheet' pursuant to § 1.121(d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic forms treated as drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Chemical or mathematical formulae, tables, and waveforms may be submitted as drawings and are subject to the same requirements as drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each chemical or mathematical formula must be labeled as a separate figure (using brackets when necessary). Waveforms must be presented as a single figure with a common vertical axis and time on horizontal axis; each waveform discussed in the specification must be identified with a separate letter designation adjacent to the vertical axis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper, single-sided use, and quality requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must be on paper that is flexible, strong, white, smooth, non-shiny, and durable; all sheets must be reasonably free from cracks, creases, and folds; only one side may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sheets must be free from erasures, alterations, overwritings, and interlineations. Photographs must be developed on paper meeting sheet-size and margin requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Size of drawing sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: All drawing sheets in an application must be the same size: either 21.0 cm by 29.7 cm (DIN A4) or 21.6 cm by 27.9 cm (8 1/2 by 11 inches).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain consistent sheet size across all drawing sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Margin and sight area requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Sheets must not contain frames around the sight and should have scan target points on two catercorner margin corners. Top margin at least 2.5 cm, left 2.5 cm, right 1.5 cm, bottom 1.0 cm, leaving specified maximum sight sizes depending on sheet size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure drawings stay within the defined sight area and margins for proper reproduction and scanning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Views: types, grouping, separation, and prohibition of projection/center lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must contain as many views as necessary (plan, elevation, section, perspective, detail views). All views must be grouped together, arranged without wasting space, clearly separated from one another, and must not be included on sheets containing specification, claims, or abstract. Views must not be connected by projection lines and must not contain center lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waveforms of electrical signals may be connected by dashed lines to show relative timing. Views should be upright and readable when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploded and partial views rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Exploded views are permissible (separated parts embraced by a bracket) and should be bracketed if on same sheet as another figure. Partial views of large machines may be broken into partial views that can be linked edge-to-edge; include a smaller scale view showing the whole and indicate positions of parts shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial views on separate sheets must be capable of edge-to-edge linkage so no partial view contains parts of another; enlarged portions must be labeled as separate views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly of multi-sheet views and very long views
rubrics_metrics.description: Where views on two or more sheets form a single complete view, the several sheets must be arranged so the complete figure can be assembled without concealing any part. Very long views may be divided into several parts stacked on a single sheet provided relationships are clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain clear and unambiguous relationships between divided parts and sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sectional view conventions and hatching
rubrics_metrics.description: Sectional view planes should be indicated on the originating view by a broken line with ends designated by numerals corresponding to the sectional view number and arrows indicating sight. Hatching must be regularly spaced oblique parallel lines, not impede reading of reference characters, and preferably at 45°.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross sections must graphically indicate material(s); same items hatched consistently; juxtaposed different elements hatched at different angles; large area hatching may be confined to edging. Different hatching types have conventional meanings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate positions and modified forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Moved or alternate positions may be shown by a broken line superimposed upon a suitable view if not crowding; otherwise use a separate view. Modified forms of construction must be shown in separate views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid crowding; present alternate and modified forms clearly and separately when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement and orientation of views and text
rubrics_metrics.description: One view must not be placed upon another or within the outline of another. All views on the same sheet should stand in the same direction and, if possible, so they can be read with the sheet held upright. Words must appear horizontal left-to-right when the page is upright or turned so the top becomes the right side, except for graphs using standard conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If views wider than sheet width are necessary, turn the sheet on its side so the top margin becomes the right-hand side.

rubrics_metrics.name: Front page view
rubrics_metrics.description: The drawing must contain as many views as necessary and one view should be suitable for inclusion on the front page of the patent application publication and patent as the illustration of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may suggest a single view (by figure number) for front-page inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale: legibility after reduction and prohibition on explicit scales
rubrics_metrics.description: The scale of a drawing must be large enough to show the mechanism without crowding when the drawing is reduced to two-thirds in reproduction. Indications such as 'actual size' or 'scale 1/2' are not permitted because they lose meaning upon reproduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design drawings to remain clear and legible at standard reproduction sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character of lines, numbers, and letters
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must be made by a process giving satisfactory reproduction characteristics: every line, number, and letter must be durable, clean, black (except color drawings), sufficiently dense and dark, uniformly thick and well-defined; weight must permit adequate reproduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirement applies to all lines including fine lines, shading, and lines representing cut surfaces. Different line thicknesses may be used where they have different meanings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shading practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Shading is encouraged if it aids understanding and does not reduce legibility; shading indicates curved surfaces; spaced lines for shading are preferred and must be thin and few in number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As substitute for shading, heavy lines on the shade side can be used except where they obscure reference characters. Light should come from the upper left at 45°. Solid black shading areas are not permitted except for bar graphs or representing color.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent use of reference characters
rubrics_metrics.description: The same part of an invention appearing in more than one view must always be designated by the same reference character, and the same reference character must never designate different parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure consistency across figures to avoid confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and approval of symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphical drawing symbols may be used for conventional elements when appropriate; elements using such symbols must be adequately identified in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Known devices should use universally recognized conventional symbols; other symbols require Office approval and must not be confused with existing symbols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of legends
rubrics_metrics.description: Suitable descriptive legends may be used subject to Office approval or may be required by the examiner where necessary for understanding of the drawing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legends should contain as few words as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbers, letters, and reference character formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference characters (preferably numerals), sheet numbers, and view numbers must be plain, legible, not enclosed within outlines, oriented in the same direction as the view, and arranged to follow the profile of the object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: English alphabet must be used except where another is customary; characters must be at least 0.32 cm (1/8 inch) in height; avoid placing them on hatched/shaded surfaces; underline reference characters in hatched areas to show clarity. Reference characters not mentioned in the description shall not appear in drawings; those mentioned must appear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead lines and their execution
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead lines between reference characters and indicated details may be straight or curved, should be as short as possible, originate near the reference character, and not cross each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead lines required for each reference character except those indicating the surface or cross section on which they are placed (such reference characters must be underlined). Lead lines must be executed in the same way as other drawing lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrows usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrows may be used at line ends provided their meaning is clear: (1) freestanding arrow on a lead line to indicate the entire section it points to; (2) arrow touching a line to indicate the surface shown by the line looking along arrow direction; (3) to show direction of movement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use arrows consistently and clearly to indicate intended meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright or mask work notice placement and size
rubrics_metrics.description: A copyright or mask work notice may appear in the drawing but must be placed within the sight of the drawing immediately below the figure representing the copyright or mask work material and be limited to letters 0.32–0.64 cm high.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content of the notice must be limited to legally provided elements (e.g., '©1983 John Doe'). Inclusion permitted only if authorization language set forth in § 1.71(e) is included at beginning of specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering of sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: Sheets of drawings should be numbered in consecutive Arabic numerals starting with 1 within the sight; numbers placed in middle top of the sheet (or right side if drawing extends close to middle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numbers must be clear and larger than reference-character numerals and shown as 'sheet_number/total_sheets' with two Arabic numerals separated by an oblique line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering of views
rubrics_metrics.description: Different views must be numbered in consecutive Arabic numerals starting with 1, independent of sheet numbering; partial views that form one complete view must be identified by same number followed by a capital letter; view numbers must be preceded by 'FIG.' except where only a single view is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If only a single view is used, it must not be numbered and 'FIG.' must not appear. View numbers must be simple, clear, and larger than reference-character numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security markings
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorized security markings may be placed on the drawings provided they are outside the sight, preferably centered in the top margin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not place security markings inside the sight area where they could interfere with reproduction or understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections on drawings must be durable
rubrics_metrics.description: Any corrections on drawings submitted to the Office must be durable and permanent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid temporary or erasable corrections; ensure permanence of any amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: No holes in drawing sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: No holes should be made by applicant in the drawing sheets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep sheets intact and free of perforations or punched holes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-references to other drawing-type rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of drawings (design drawings, international design, plant drawings, reissue drawings, reproductions) are governed by specific other sections (§ 1.152, § 1.1026, § 1.165, § 1.173(a)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the referenced sections for specialized drawing rules applicable to those categories.
